Title: Putin conveys warm regards to Sultan Ibrahim, praises strong Malaysia-Russia relations
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Russian President Vladimir Putin conveyed his warm regards to His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, during a bilateral meeting with Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim yesterday.
"We had the pleasure of meeting in Moscow this May at the celebrations of the 81st anniversary of Victory," Putin said during the meeting held on the sidelines of the 18th BRICS Summit in New Delhi, India, according to a transcript on the Kremlin's website.
"We highly appreciate the high level and truly friendly nature of relations between Russia and Malaysia."
Earlier, Bernama reported that Anwar conveyed warm regards from Sultan Ibrahim to the Russian president and reiterated His Majesty's invitation to Putin to undertake a state visit to Malaysia.
Sultan Ibrahim, who ascended the federal throne on Jan 31, 2024, has visited Russia three times: a state visit in August 2025, a special visit in January 2026, and a visit to Moscow in May for Russia's Victory Day celebrations.
Meanwhile, Putin noted during the meeting that both countries would mark 60 years of diplomatic relations next year.
He expressed hope to reach the milestone with a wealth of positive experience and a solid foundation for further expansion.
"Contacts are developing dynamically across the security councils, parliaments, foreign ministries, and other relevant agencies.
"Recently, in August, the fifth meeting of the Joint Russian-Malaysian Commission on Economic, Scientific, Technical and Cultural Cooperation was held in Vladivostok."
He added that Russia attached great importance to bilateral cooperation in education, science, technology, and tourism.
Putin also noted that bilateral trade had increased by 12.9 per cent last year, describing it as an encouraging figure.

Title: SC proposes sukuk framework for climate resilience
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Securities Commission (SC) has proposed a new purpose-driven sukuk framework aimed at mobilising capital for climate adaptation, resilience and sustainable development, as the country faces growing exposure to climate-related risks.
SC chairman Datuk Mohammad Faiz Azmi said the proposed framework, to be known as Sukuk Prisma SDG, would build on Malaysia's existing Sustainable and Responsible Investment (SRI) sukuk framework.
The proposal was unveiled at the 17th SC-Oxford Centre for Islamic Studies (OCIS) Roundtable 2026, themed "Building Resilience: The Intersection between Capital, Climate and Innovation", held in Oxford, United Kingdom, today.
Also present were the Sultan of Perak, Sultan Nazrin Muizzuddin Shah, and OCIS director Dr Farhan Nizami.
"The idea is to focus on non-ringgit sukuk issuances that translate national priorities into clear, credible and globally recognisable purposes under the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)," he said in his opening remarks.
Mohammad Faiz said the framework would be Shariah-based and aligned with the SC's Maqasid al-Shariah Guidance, while also adopting the Asean Taxonomy and international green bond principles.
He said the proposal was still a work in progress and the SC welcomed feedback from participants at the roundtable.
The initiative comes as Malaysia seeks to scale up financing for climate adaptation and resilience amid increasing losses from extreme weather events.
Mohammad Faiz said Malaysia, located in a climate-vulnerable region, had suffered more than US$2.2 billion (RM8.95 billion) in losses from floods — its main climate risk — over the past five years.
"These temperatures are not simply statistics or mere projections. They signal a change that will have profound implications for infrastructure, investments and our resilience," he said.
He said sustainable and responsible finance would be critical in facilitating the funding needed to help economies adapt to and mitigate the effects of climate change.
However, he said stronger market infrastructure and clearer adaptation-focused frameworks were needed to measure and verify outcomes.
"Without these foundations, scaling private capital towards climate resilience will remain constrained because investors cannot underwrite what they cannot measure," he said.
Mohammad Faiz said Malaysia was not starting from scratch, having built a comprehensive ecosystem for sustainable finance.
He said outstanding SRI sukuk had grown from US$1.3 billion in 2020 to US$12.9 billion last year, while Malaysia ranked among the region's top three issuers of green, social, sustainability and sustainability-linked bonds and sukuk.
This accounted for about a quarter of total regional issuances, he said.
Under the SC's Capital Market Masterplan 2026-2030, Malaysia aims to mobilise about US$24.6 billion over five years towards climate transition, adaptation, resilience and social development initiatives.
Mohammad Faiz said the roundtable would focus on identifying scalable and investable solutions capable of delivering measurable resilience outcomes.
He said this could include outcome-linked and resilience-based sukuk, blended finance and other innovative structures to improve the bankability of adaptation investments.
"Our task over the next two days is to develop workable proposals for the wider world to use within the ambit of financing climate adaptation and resilience and Islamic finance," he said.

Title: Take control of what we put into our lungs
Article:
LETTERS:
Haze is far more than a seasonal nuisance.
Treating it as a temporary inconvenience risks underestimating the harm it can cause.
Behind Air Pollutant Index (API) numbers are real people, including children going to school, workers commuting to the office, elderly people going about daily routines and individuals with respiratory and cardiovascular problems trying to breathe normally.
This is why people are repeatedly advised to reduce outdoor activities when air quality deteriorates.
But there is an uncomfortable question we cannot ignore. Why expose our lungs to cigarette smoke when the air around us is already polluted?
Cigarette smoke contains thousands of chemicals that can damage the lungs and cardiovascular system.
During a haze episode, continuing to smoke adds another source of harmful pollutants to an already compromised respiratory environment.
It is, quite simply, a double burden on the lungs. The danger does not stop with smokers.
Second-hand smoke exposes family members, colleagues and members of the public to harmful substances.
For smokers, the haze should therefore be viewed not only as a reason to stay indoors but also as a reason to quit. This is where public health messaging must become more integrated.
When authorities advise people to monitor API readings, limit outdoor activities and protect vulnerable groups, tobacco control should be part of that conversation.
A haze episode should be treated as a powerful teachable moment. If people are concerned about breathing polluted air from the environment, they should also recognise the additional harm caused by inhaling cigarette smoke.
The responsibility, however, does not rest entirely with individuals. Government agencies, healthcare professionals, employers, schools and universities must get involved.
Breathing polluted air should never become normal. Nor should smoking during the haze be dismissed as an individual's personal choice.
DR MOHD ROZAIMY RIDZUAN

Faculty of Administrative Science and Policy Studies

Title: Anwar looks forward to meeting India's Grand Mufti during Keralam visit
Article:
KERALAM: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim is looking forward to meeting India's Grand Mufti Sheikh Abubakr Ahmad during his visit to Keralam tomorrow, following his participation in the 18th BRICS Leaders' Summit.
Responding to a message from Sheikh Abubakr Ahmad welcoming him and the Malaysian delegation to India, Anwar expressed his gratitude to the Grand Mufti.
"Thank you for your warm wishes, Sheikh. I look forward to seeing you tomorrow, Insya-Allah," Anwar posted on Facebook today.
Sheikh Abubakr Ahmad had earlier expressed particular appreciation for Anwar's decision to include Jamia Markaz, one of India's premier Islamic institutions, in his itinerary.
"Your commitment to exchanging views on community development, education, and religious affairs reflects a shared vision for intellectual and societal progress," the Grand Mufti said.
"May this historic visit and bilateral dialogue open vibrant new pathways in higher education, social empowerment, and cultural connectivity between Malaysia and India, particularly fostering stronger ties with Keralam," he added.
Anwar, who is also finance minister, arrived in New Delhi on Friday to attend the 18th BRICS Leaders' Summit hosted by Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi.
Following the completion of his visit to Keralam, the prime minister is scheduled to depart for the Maldives on Sept 14.

Title: Calicut in focus ahead of Anwar's visit to Keralam after BRICS Summit
Article:
KERALAM: The historic city of Calicut, also known as Kozhikode, in Keralam is drawing international attention ahead of Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim's visit tomorrow, following his participation in the 18th BRICS Summit.
A check around Calicut today showed the city bustling with daily activities as interest in the prime minister's arrival built following the release of his official itinerary.
Anwar is scheduled to meet India's Grand Mufti Sheikh Abubakr Ahmad tomorrow to exchange views on community development, educational advancement, and interfaith harmony.
On Monday, the prime minister will meet Keralam Chief Minister V. D. Satheesan and Keralam Governor Rajendra Vishwanath Arlekar to strengthen bilateral cooperation in key sectors, including trade, investment, tourism, healthcare, and education.
The presence of the Malaysian delegation and media coverage surrounding the prime minister's itinerary have placed Calicut in focus during his visit to southern India.
Calicut has a rich history as a major trading hub and was once a vital port along the Malabar Coast, renowned for its spice trade with international merchants.
The city also holds a prominent place in global history following Portuguese navigator Vasco da Gama's landing at nearby Kappad beach in 1498 with three ships and 170 crew members, marking the European discovery of the sea route to India. A monument at Kappad commemorates the historic arrival.
Anwar arrived in New Delhi on Friday to attend the 18th BRICS Leaders' Summit hosted by Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi.
On the sidelines of the summit, Anwar held bilateral meetings with Modi at Hyderabad House, as well as Russian President Vladimir Putin, Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian, and Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed.
Following his visit to Keralam, the prime minister is scheduled to depart for the Maldives on Sept 14.

Title: Family appeals for Smart team to stay, continue Nepal search
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: The family of missing Malaysian hiker Muhammad Muhaimin Azhad Noor Hadi, 27, has urged the Special Malaysia Disaster Assistance and Rescue Team (Smart) to continue the search and rescue (SAR) operation in Nepal.
The family said they were disappointed and frustrated after learning that the Smart team involved in the flood relief mission in Nepal was expected to
return
to Malaysia soon.
Muhaimin was reported to have been hiking in Langtang Valley with two friends, Muhammad Adib Haikal Awang Mansor, 27, and Muhammad Zaki Othman, 29, before they went missing during the Aug 26 disaster.
His father, Noor Hadi Mohd Hassan, 62, questioned the decision to withdraw the team, saying the reasons and details of the operation had not been clearly explained.
"We were shocked and disappointed by the decision because we do not know how the process took place, including how the assets were withdrawn.
"We also wonder whether no further action can be taken, such as searching the affected villages.
"Until now, we do not know how the search was conducted. They said efforts had been made, but we do not know how extensive the search was," he told reporters at his home in Taman Tun Sardon here today.
Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan previously said the Smart team deployed for the Humanitarian Assistance and Disaster Relief (HADR) mission in Nepal was expected to return to Malaysia today or tomorrow.
The 11-member team departed for Nepal on Sept 4 aboard a Royal Malaysian Air Force (RMAF) A400M aircraft.
Noor Hadi said the family and relatives were appealing for the search to continue.
"If they are still alive, Alhamdulillah. But if not, we still want certainty. We hope the government will take this seriously and find the best way to resolve the situation.
"My health has deteriorated since the incident because I am worried and constantly thinking about my son. He has also been the one helping me with my movements," said Noor Hadi, who uses a wheelchair after losing one leg.
Muhaimin's mother, Zaleha Ariffin, 57, said she would accept whatever fate had been determined for her son but wanted a clear conclusion so the family would not be left waiting indefinitely.
"He is still young. He had told us several times that he wanted to get engaged and marry his chosen partner next year.
"He should be counting down the days to his happy occasion, but this is what has happened. We are deeply worried. I sincerely hope the authorities will make every effort to find him and bring him home," she said.
Meanwhile, Muhaimin's girlfriend, who declined to be named, said their last WhatsApp conversation was at 11am Malaysian time, about five minutes before the incident occurred at 8.45am Nepal time.
"He told me he had eaten chapati that day before contact was lost. I thought he had entered a forested area.
"Not long after that, I saw news of the incident on social media and informed Muhammad Muhaimin's family," she said.

Title: Indian woman drowns after falling from boat during Tioman diving trip
Article:
KUANTAN, Sept 13 —  An Indian national drowned after she was believed to have slipped off a boat following a scuba diving activity in the waters of Renggis, Pulau Tioman in Rompin yesterday.
Rompin district police chief Supt Sharif Shai Sharif Mondoi said police received a call from the Tekek Health Clinic at about 10 am regarding the drowning of Sabiya Shiek, 65.
He said initial investigations revealed the victim had taken part in a discovery scuba diving session with six family members, accompanied by two instructors and a dive master.
“After the session, the victim informed the instructor that she wished to return to the boat.
“However, after her child helped remove her diving gear, Sabiya is believed to have slipped while climbing the ladder to get on board and fell back into the sea,” he said in a statement yesterday.
He said diving instructors launched an immediate search and located the victim about 15 minutes later, lying unconscious on the sandy seabed near the dive site.
The victim was taken to the Tekek Health Clinic on Pulau Tioman, where a medical officer pronounced her dead, with a post-mortem scheduled at the Tengku Ampuan Afzan Hospital here on Monday. — Bernama

Title: Thai man drowns in Sungai Golok near Malaysia-Thailand border
Article:
OTA BHARU, Sept 13 — A 23-year-old Thai man was found drowned in Sungai Golok along the Malaysia-Thailand border near Kampung Pengkalan Pasir and Abe Yie in Rantau Panjang, Pasir Mas yesterday evening.
Rantau Panjang Fire and Rescue Station chief Hamzah Musa said the victim, Faiz Hasan, was found by Thai authorities at 7.10 pm while a search and rescue operation was underway.
“We received a call from the General Operations Force (GOF) at 6.27 am yesterday regarding an incident in which a person had jumped into the water and did not resurface.
“The search and rescue operation along the riverbank began as early as 7 am before resuming today, involving eight personnel from the Rantau Panjang Fire and Rescue Station, with assistance from several agencies, including the police and a diving unit from Thailand,” he said in a statement.
Hamzah said the victim’s body was taken by Thai authorities for further action, while the search and rescue operation was fully called off at 7.15 pm today. — Bernama

Title: Anwar says Malaysia set to gain from new investment, industrial cooperation with India
Article:
NEW DELHI, Sept 13 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said his meetings with representatives of several leading companies here today reflect the continued confidence of industry players and investors in Malaysia’s economic potential and direction.
“The Madani Government will continue to facilitate quality investments that strengthen local industries, create high-value jobs, and ensure that the benefits are felt by the people,” he said.
Anwar, who is also Finance Minister, met representatives of DRB-Hicom, Segula Technologies India, AWL Agri Business Ltd and Motherson Group to discuss opportunities to expand investment and industrial cooperation between Malaysia and India in strategic sectors.
The first meeting was held with representatives of DRB-Hicom, who were accompanied by their strategic partners, to explore opportunities for cooperation with the automotive industry in India.
“I then met with the leadership of Segula Technologies India, a global engineering and technology company, which expressed the intention to establish a global engineering centre in Malaysia by the end of 2026,” he said in a post on social media.
The initiative, he said, could strengthen Malaysia’s local engineering capabilities through the hiring of Malaysian talent and the application of artificial intelligence expertise in the automotive, aerospace, energy and advanced manufacturing sectors.
Meanwhile, the meeting with AWL Agri Business Ltd, one of the major companies in India’s agribusiness sector, explored efforts to increase its purchase of products from Malaysian suppliers, Anwar said.
The company has imported about RM1.5 billion worth of Malaysian palm oil products, creating opportunities to expand cooperation in palm oil, specialty fats, oleochemicals and other downstream products.
“I also met with representatives of Motherson Group, who shared plans to expand their information technology and digital solutions business in Malaysia,” the Prime Minister said.
The move would leverage on the strengths of local talent, Malaysia’s digital infrastructure, and the country’s strategic position as a gateway to regional markets, he added.
Anwar arrived here on Friday to attend the 18th BRICS Leaders’ Summit. This is his second visit to India in his capacity as Prime Minister, following his visit in August 2024. — Bernama

Title: Anwar to outline Malaysia’s vision for inclusive global growth at Brics summit
Article:
NEW DELHI, Sept 13 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim is  scheduled to deliver a National Statement on Shaping the Future for Inclusive Global Growth at the 18th Brics Leaders’ Summit here today.
He is expected to emphasise the importance of strengthening cooperation among Brics member and partner countries in addressing development challenges, expanding economic opportunities and ensuring that the benefits of technological advancement and innovation are enjoyed more inclusively by all countries.
