In Keralam, he will meet with the Grand Mufti of India, Sheikh Abubakr Ahmad, to exchange perspectives on community development, educational advancement, and interfaith harmony.
As part of the visit, the Prime Minister is scheduled to meet Chief Minister Thiru V. D. Satheesan and Governor of Keralam Thiru Rajendra Vishwanath Arleka.
The engagements aim to strengthen bilateral cooperation between Malaysia and the state of Keralam across key sectors such as trade and investment, tourism, healthcare and education.
On Sept 14, Anwar will head to the Maldives. — Bernama

Title: From dishwasher in Melbourne to heading the kitchen at Gilda in George Town, a Malaysian (food) love story
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Sept 13 — Before he was brining chicken and making coconut milk-laced romesco at Gilda Restaurant, Ahmad Soffian Salim was washing plates in restaurants more than 14 years ago.
It was almost an accidental career change for the mechanical engineering major who had initially worked in the engineering department at Malaysia Airlines planning aircraft maintenance and servicing.
Ahmad relocated to Melbourne, Australia with his wife, Aim Aris, back in 2012 when the latter was pursuing her postgraduate studies there.
Living in an area that was far from the airport, Ahmad sought out jobs near their home and ended up as a kitchen assistant washing dishes and pots in a restaurant.
Chef Ahmad working in the open kitchen.
”We lived in an area where one of the best cafes in Melbourne was just behind our house,” Aim said.
She said 2012 was the peak of cafe culture in the area and it was their first time experiencing the Australian hospitality industry where in some cafes, the chef designs the menu to pair with coffee.
”It was really interesting and that was the first spark for Ahmad to want to try immersing himself in this industry,” she said.
One of the easiest ways to get in was to work his way up so that was how Ahmad started working as a kitchen assistant.
”I love food but what really made me want to be a chef was the high quality local produce there,” Ahmad said.
Gilda Lunch Spread is meant for sharing.
He said the locally sourced produce was of such good quality that the chefs did not really need to do much except to elevate it and let its natural flavours come through.
The couple had only expected to stay in Melbourne for about two years but it somehow stretched into eight as Ahmad worked his way up from a kitchen assistant to line cook to becoming the head chef of an Australian restaurant in five years.
“I worked in different cafes and restaurants and trained in modern Australian cuisine as my interest in cooking grew,” he said.
He had briefly considered applying to study in a culinary school but the fees were high while chefs in the restaurants he worked in encouraged him to learn on the job instead.
So, he took jobs in different kitchens to build his experience, going from working a morning shift in one restaurant and heading to another restaurant for dinner service.
Clockwise from left: Grilled sea bass, grilled chicken and roasted mushroom baguette.
“I was fully occupied working from morning until night time for five days kind of thing, I often worked two jobs during that time because I wanted to learn,” he said.
His appetite for learning was fuelled by what he found around him in Melbourne: cafes, restaurants, coffee and ingredients that opened up new possibilities.
After working his way up to become head chef and with Aim nearing the end of her PhD in late 2019, they decided to take one year off to travel and set up pop-up kitchens and collaborations in Jakarta, Hong Kong, Japan and Thailand.
However, the Covid-19 pandemic disrupted their plans.
The couple was in Penang to conduct research and work on a cookbook project in 2020.
“We managed to do our pop-up for three days—a kitchen takeover—at Norm Micro Roastery. And then the government announced a lockdown,” Ahmad said.
Interstate and international travel were prohibited and their plans to continue to Europe were put on hold.
It was then that they were asked to help plan a restaurant menu as a restaurant consultant.
Chef Ahmad and wife Aim manage the restaurant which is co-founded with three other investors.
“At that point, I had only ever been a chef, I didn’t know much about restaurant consultancy so we told the restaurant, we will try,” he recalled.
What was initially meant to be a month of assistance became nine months as they developed the menu, helped run the kitchen and trained the team.
For Ahmad, it was also his first experience working as a chef in Malaysia.
Aim said they decided to make the most of their circumstances since they were both stranded in Penang during the lockdown.
From the one consultancy project, it led to more projects including a one-year residency at a restaurant in Chinatown in Kuala Lumpur in 2023.
The residency gave Ahmad something he had missed while setting up kitchens for others: a kitchen where he could cook his own food with his own team.
They later helped with the menu planning, training and opening of Peninsula House in Penang in July 2024, before handing over to its team.
The birth of Gilda
After years of moving between projects, they started toying with the idea of opening their own restaurant.
”Since we are both from KL, our initial plan was to set up a place there,” Aim said.
Penang, however, had another connection waiting for them — a friendship formed through a small pop-up during the pandemic.
Gilda offers contemporary dining from brunch to dinner.
Among the guests was art collector and founder of Blank Canvas, Leong KY, who was also stranded in Penang at the time.
He subsequently invited the couple to cook for private dinners and gallery events in Penang.
“I would say he is our ‘lockdown friend’,” Ahmad said.
When Leong found a new space for Blank Canvas in Soo Hong Lane, it was larger than he needed.
He reached out to Ahmad and suggested they use the extra space beside the gallery as a restaurant.
They initially offered to consult instead but Leong wanted them to run and manage the place.
The idea gradually took hold. Their Penang project progressed while their Kuala Lumpur plans were delayed, prompting them to focus on Gilda.
The restaurant opened on October 25 last year, with five founders: Ahmad, Aim, Leong, Alfred Cheong and property owner Dickson Lim.
Ahmad and Aim oversee operations, while the space also doubles as a showcase of artworks from Leong’s personal collection.
”I chose the name Gilda because I wanted something short, easy to read and with the character of a female name, as I noticed Melbourne restaurants tend to use female names,” she said.
She said the word is old English for golden and gold is a good thing to associate with the restaurant as in terms of food, it also refers to golden crust, the crispness of cooking, the golden standard or food that is really nice.
At Gilda, Ahmad’s food reflects the kitchens he learnt in, without restricting him to a single cuisine.
His foundation is modern Australian cooking, which he sees as shaped by the food, traditions and cultures brought by migrants.
Back in Malaysia, Southe-ast Asian flavours naturally became part of that mix.
“And safe to say the direction is more like we want to make good food, without any limitation, without any box,” he said.
One of the items on the menu is a sea bass served with Ahmad’s take on romesco that incorporates green chilli and coconut milk.
Alongside it is a kerabu-like salad with mango and edamame, bringing another combination of influences to the plate.
He said the menu he planned focused on layering of flavours with Malaysian influences.
Aim said Gilda not only offers contemporary dining but is a neo bistro with items for brunch and small plates for customers who just want to hang out with their friends and family.
Gilda is open from Thursday to Monday from 11am to 4.30pm and 5.30pm to 10pm. Reservations can be made at
https://gildadining.com.

Title: Temiar facial art tradition embraces a modern touch while preserving its heritage
Article:
GUA MUSANG, Sept 13 — Lipstick and face powder may have replaced charcoal and limestone paste in the beauty routines of the Orang Asli from the Temiar tribe, but modernisation has not erased the centuries-old tradition of facial adornment passed down through generations.
Endah Angah, 37, said the practice of painting geometric motifs, including long and wavy lines and dots, on the face remained deeply cherished by her community as an enduring symbol of its cultural heritage.
She said the growing difficulty of sourcing traditional beauty ingredients such as kesumba seeds had led her community to increasingly rely on modern cosmetics, which were easier to obtain than having to venture into the forest in search of the natural materials.
“In the past, these natural ingredients were easy to find, so we didn’t have to go deep into the forest to look for them. But now, they’re getting harder to find.
“Using modern cosmetics is much easier for us. The red and black colours from lipstick and eyeliner also make the patterns on our faces look neater and brighter, and they last longer too,” the housewife told
Bernama
recently.
Rahimah Punai, 39, said modern cosmetics might have changed the way the facial motifs were created, but their spiritual meaning and connection to their ancestral heritage remained intact.
“We make sure every horizontal and wavy line, as well as every dot, is drawn carefully because each one has its own meaning. The lines represent the river, while the dots symbolise our connection to nature.
“Nothing has changed, except that we now use modern cosmetics. We have to follow what our ancestors passed down to us and keep it the same to preserve our customs and heritage. So, we cannot just add streaks to the forehead, nose or cheeks,” she said.
Abong Busu, 55, said the custom remained deeply rooted among the Temiar tribe and continued to be practised during religious ceremonies such as the sewang and at community gatherings.
“This is how we introduce the tradition to the younger generation. The children are very interested and often ask us a lot of questions about it,” she said.
Meanwhile, Kelantan State Department for Culture and Arts (JKKN) director Rohaniza Abdullah said the use of modern cosmetics, while retaining the original facial motifs, represented a new way of preserving and continuing the traditional heritage practice.
She said creativity in producing modern-style facial decorations was a way to keep the heritage relevant while preserving its originality and aesthetic value as an important part of Orang Asli identity and socio-cultural life.
“The use of modern cosmetics is a positive development for the community because the traditional facial motifs can still be recreated while retaining their original patterns and colours. This also helps preserve the tradition for future generations.
“Preserving this tradition for the next generation is important, so efforts by various parties, especially to engage young people, must continue,” she said.
Rohaniza added that the uniqueness and symbolism behind the facial motifs could make the traditional art an iconic representation of Orang Asli culture. — Bernama

Title: Social media overtakes TV, news websites as Malaysians’ main source of news
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 12 — News consumption has reached a turning point: social media now edges television and news websites as the most widely used source of news.
This changing mix of traditional and digital news sources is reflected in the 2026 edition of the annual Digital News Report, published by the Reuters Institute for the Study of Journalism.
Across the 48 markets covered in 2026, social media was the most widely used source of news, averaging 54 per cent. Television followed at 52 per cent, while news websites were used by 51 per cent.
In 2017, television led at 73 per cent and news websites at 69 per cent, while social media stood at 54 per cent. Its move into first place therefore reflects the decline of the other two sources more than long-term growth in its own reach.
Social media dominates Malaysia’s news mix
Malaysia’s shift is even more pronounced. Nearly seven in 10 respondents used social media for news in 2026, compared with 42 per cent for news websites and 36 per cent for television.
What stands out over the decade is not the growth of social media, which has remained above 60 per cent since 2017, but the retreat of established news channels.
News website use fell 24 per centage points and television dropped 18 points. Print recorded the steepest fall at 31 points.
Radio remained a smaller and more volatile source, reaching 23 per cent in 2026.
Among Malaysian respondents overall, AI chatbot use stood at 11 per cent in 2026, compared with nine per cent in 2025. Podcast use was eight percent, compared with nine percent the year before. With only two years of data available for both, it is too early to establish a longer-term direction.
Social media is not only where Malaysians consume news. Increasingly, it is how they find it.
In 2026, 63 per cent discovered news through social media, compared with 44 per cent through search engines and just 27 per cent through direct visits to news websites and apps.
Other routes remained less common, with news aggregators and mobile alerts both at 20 per cent, while email stood at 12 per cent.
Taken together, the figures suggest that the change is not simply a move from traditional to digital media. Social media now plays a dual role: it is both a source of news and the main route through which Malaysians discover it.
WhatsApp and video platforms gain ground
The platforms carrying that news are changing too.
WhatsApp overtook Facebook as Malaysia’s most widely used platform for news in 2026, although only narrowly, at 50 per cent versus 49 per cent.
The bigger shift, however, has been towards video. TikTok surged from just two per cent in 2019 to 45 per cent in 2026, while YouTube climbed from 26 per cent to 41 per cent over the decade.
Together, their growth points to video becoming a much larger part of how Malaysians find, watch and share news.
The platform mix also continues to change. Threads reached 11 per cent in 2026 after appearing in the survey at two per cent in 2024, while X fell to nine percent after peaking at 22 per cent in 2022.
That growing dependence on social platforms also raises a harder question: how carefully are users checking what reaches them?
The Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission’s Internet Users Survey 2024 found that 61.5 per cent of internet users shared news, while the proportion checking its validity and source reliability fell from 79.2 per cent to 70.7 per cent.
The survey also noted growing reliance on automated or platform-based fact-checking. It added that trust in online content was declining amid the rise of fake news, particularly political and health misinformation.
News habits differ by age and gender
Social media crossed generations, with usage ranging from 65 to 71 per cent across every age group in 2026.
The sharper differences appeared in the use of other news sources. Respondents aged 55 and above recorded higher use of news websites, television, radio and print than younger age groups, while younger Malaysians were more likely to turn to newer formats.
That contrast was especially clear with AI chatbots. Twenty-one per cent who use them in 2026 were among those aged 18 to 24. A mere six per cent of the respondents were aged 45 and above.
Podcast use showed a similar, though less pronounced, pattern, with younger respondents recording the highest use.
The age divide was therefore not a simple split between digital and traditional media. Older Malaysians remained active on social media while continuing to use established news sources at higher rates, whereas younger users were more likely to add newer formats such as AI chatbots and podcasts to their news habits.
A study of Malaysian Generation Z published in Media Asia identified virality, news awareness, the ubiquity of news and credibility as themes in how participants understood news. The findings offer some context for a media environment in which news appears alongside entertainment, personal updates and commentary rather than occupying a space of its own.
Gender differences were modest for social media but considerably wider for some established news sources.
Social media use was almost identical among women and men, at 69 and 68 per cent respectively. News websites showed the biggest gap, however, reaching 48 per cent of men compared with 36 percent of women.
The pattern was less pronounced for AI chatbots. In 2026, they were used for news by 12 perc ent of men and 11 per cent of women, after use among women rose from seven per cent the previous year. Podcast use showed a wider difference, at 10 per cent among men and six per cent among women.
For Malaysians, the shift today is not simply about where news is consumed, but how it is discovered, shared and encountered. Traditional sources remain important, especially among older audiences, but social platforms now play a much greater role in determining what news reaches people in the first place.
Note on the data:
The Digital News Report is based on annual online surveys conducted by YouGov. For the 2026 edition, fieldwork was carried out between mid-January and the end of February. The Malaysian sample comprised 2,076 respondents, while annual samples from 2017 to 2026 ranged from 2,004 to 2,108 respondents.
The number of markets covered increased from 36 in 2017 to 48 in 2025 and 2026, meaning the international trend figures are annual averages across the markets surveyed rather than a fixed group. Respondents could select more than one news source, so the figures do not add up to 100 per cent or represent market shares.
— Bernama

Title: Sarawak police close final chapter as Long Lellang crash victims return to families
Article:
MIRI, Sept 12 — The remains of all five victims of the Sept 8 helicopter crash in Long Lellang have been handed over to their respective families, said Sarawak Police Commissioner Datuk Mohamad Zainal Abdullah.
He said the remaining process involved identifying the victims’ personal belongings for handover to their families.
“Alhamdulillah, I have just come out of the Forensic Department and we are now carrying out the identification process of the personal belongings to be handed over to the families.
“Technically, we have handed everything over (remains of the victims), but there may be some issues with arranging the aircraft, so they may be flown out tomorrow (Sept 13).
“As far as the police are concerned, we have handed the victims over to their families for further arrangements,” he told reporters outside the Miri Hospital mortuary today.
He said two of the victims would be flown to Peninsular Malaysia, while the other three would be buried in Miri and Kuching.
Flight arrangements and related matters would be handled by Layang-Layang Aerospace Sdn Bhd, he added.
“The respective families will liaise with Layang-Layang Aerospace. As far as the police are concerned, we have handed all the victims over to their families for the next process, including the flight arrangements,” he said.
On the cause of the crash, Mohamad Zainal said the matter would be announced by the Air Accident Investigation Bureau.
As for the police investigation, he said the case had been classified as a Sudden Death Report (SDR), with statements from 19 witnesses recorded so far.
“I will provide further updates later,” he said.
Mohamad Zainal also thanked the Department of Chemistry Malaysia for working tirelessly to complete the DNA identification process within 24 hours.
“As early as 6am today, they informed us that the DNA samples had been analysed and matched the markings we made at the scene with the victims we had identified,” he said.
The helicopter, operated under the Flying Doctor Service (FDS), crashed at the Long Lellang STOLport at about 3.40pm on Sept 8, killing all five people on board.
The victims were pilot Capt Zainol Afiq Bee Sham, 30; medical officer Dr Ainul Baraah Kamaruddin, 33; assistant medical officer Alexson Adit Henry, 31; and staff nurses Debra Moset, 40, and Jessie Paya Jok, 44.
Dr Ainul’s remains are expected to be flown to Kelantan, while Capt Zainol’s remains are expected to be flown to Kuala Lumpur at 8.30am tomorrow (Sept 13). Debra’s remains are expected to be airlifted to Kuching at about 9am.
Dr Ainul is expected to be buried at the Sri Kedeper Muslim Cemetery in Kota Bharu, while Capt Zainol’s remains will be brought to his home state of Negeri Sembilan.
Alexson Adit is expected to be laid to rest at the Anglican Cemetery in Lambir, while Jessie Paya is expected to be buried at the Borneo Evangelical Mission (BEM) cemetery, also in Lambir.
Meanwhile, Debra’s remains are expected to be transported to her family home in Kampung Semadang, Padawan, Kuching. — The Borneo Post

Title: Home Ministry to announce effective date for citizenship amendments once ready
Article:
KULIM, Sept 12 — The Home Ministry (KDN) will announce the effective date of amendments to citizenship provisions for children born overseas to Malaysian women once all preparations for their implementation have been completed.
Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said the preparations included the relevant documentation, citizenship regulations and an online application system, which would also involve Malaysian representative offices worldwide.
He said the effective date had been determined by the Yang di-Pertuan Agong and KDN would announce it once several administrative matters had been finalised.
“At the ministry level (KDN), all preparations have been completed, including the relevant documents and citizenship regulations. We have also obtained confirmation from the Attorney General’s Chambers.
“The preparations also involve setting up the online application system as its implementation will involve Malaysian representative offices around the world,” he told reporters at a meet-and-greet event at his service centre here today.
He said the implementation of the amendments was expected to provide significant relief to Malaysian women or mothers who had been waiting for the citizenship process for their children born overseas.
He said that out of approximately 50,000 outstanding citizenship applications that previously needed to be processed, about 7,000 involved children born overseas to Malaysian mothers.
“Of the 7,000, only hundreds remain undecided as we are still processing the old applications while waiting for the amendments to come into force,” he said.
He said once the amendments came into force and new applications were opened, applications under the category would be processed in accordance with the new provisions.
Meanwhile, Saifuddin Nasution said KDN is continuing efforts to resolve the remaining 4,121 citizenship applications out of the original 50,000 outstanding applications, with a target of deciding on all of them this year.
He said the four main categories with the highest number of applications were under Article 15A, Article 15(2), Article 19(1) and Article 30(1) of the Federal Constitution. — Bernama

Title: Zahid says door for Umno-PAS cooperation ‘wide open’, eyes million-strong unity rally ahead of GE16
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 12 — The presence of PAS leaders at this year’s Umno general assembly signals the potential for Malaysia’s two largest Malay-based parties to cooperate again, Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said today.
The Umno president said the gesture indicated that the room for friendship between both parties was now wide open and must be further strengthened before the GE16.
“God willing, we will be open for a
tahaluf siyasi
with them,” Zahid said in his winding-up speech.
The Arabic term means political understanding.
PAS secretary-general Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan led a delegation of his party leaders to the Umno assembly opening yesterday.
Zahid also instructed Umno Youth chief Datuk Dr Muhamad Akmal Saleh to work with his counterparts in PAS and gather over a million Malay-Muslims for a mammoth rally he dubbed “Himpunan Perpaduan Ummah”.
“Akmal, I am giving you the mandate. Work with them well. Mobilise roadshows in every state in the days leading to the mammoth rally,” he said.
After the 2018 general election, Umno and PAS entered a short-lived political cooperation called Muafakat Nasional and were part of the federal government led by Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin, followed by Datuk Seri Ismail Sabri Yaakob between March 2020 and October 2022.
The Umno-led Barisan Nasional coalition later switched support to Pakatan Harapan and formed the unity government after the 15th general election in November 2022.
Both Umno and PAS currently govern Negeri Sembilan together, after all parties fell short of securing a simple majority in the recent state polls — a power-sharing arrangement that Zahid’s remarks today suggests he wants to see replicated on a bigger scale ahead of GE16.

Title: Umno’s exit from unity govt would demand fresh mandate, not backroom deal, says Zahid
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 12 — Umno president Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said today that the party's removal from the unity government would require a fresh mandate to determine the country's next administration.
He said there would be only two options if Umno were asked to leave the government: hold a general election to obtain a fresh mandate, or formally remove the party and hold a vote of no confidence in the Dewan Rakyat.
“If we are asked to leave, logically, the original basis of 112 seats would no longer exist. A new mandate should be obtained.
“There are only two choices. One is to obtain the mandate again by holding a general election. The second is to officially remove us and hold a vote of no confidence in the Dewan Rakyat,” he
said in his closing speech at the Umno general assembly here.
His remarks drew loud chants of “
Bubar!
” – meaning “dissolve” in Malay – from delegates in the hall.
Zahid said the original 112-seat basis comprised 82 seats held by Pakatan Harapan and 30 by Barisan Nasional (BN) before other parties subsequently joined the administration.
He also pointed out that three PKR lawmakers, Datuk Seri Rafizi Ramli, Nik Nazmi Nik Ahmad and Wong Chen, had since left the party.
Zahid’s remarks came after he criticised cybertroopers loyal to PKR, nicknamed “Ceplos” by Rafizi, who have called for Umno to leave the unity government, challenging them to act on their demands.
“Don't ask us to leave the government. They challenge us, saying, ‘Leave the government if you dare.’ Remember, the Malaysian unity government exists because of Umno, and the prime minister became prime minister because of Umno's support,” he said.
“Do you have the courage? If you do, throw us out quickly. If you do, dissolve quickly,” Zahid said.
He also questioned the use of the term ‘Madani government’, saying the agreement for the administration under Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, was to refer to it as the ‘unity government’.
Zahid then read aloud the definition of a unity government from a piece of paper he was holding, telling his critics to look at the document.
Yesterday, Zahid called for the 16th general election to be held as soon as possible, saying BN should not wait until the last possible moment to seek a fresh mandate from voters.
At the end of his speech, he told delegates that this would be the last general assembly before GE16.

Title: ‘One for you, one for me’: Tok Mat calls for PAS to put its unity talk to the test after Melaka election
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 12 — Umno should press for snap elections in one of the four states ruled by Perikatan Nasional to test the sincerity of PAS, Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan said today.
Mohamad, popularly known as Tok Mat, said the era of one-party rule was over, but Umno should not let other parties take advantage of its generosity in political pacts.
“So, after the Melaka polls, I want to ask the president to test the sincerity of our friends.
“Ask them to hold elections in one of the SG4 states,” the Umno deputy president said, using the initials for the four state governments controlled by PAS — Kelantan, Terengganu, Kedah and Perlis.
“If they are really sincere about uniting the Malays, let us see what formula they would resort to.
“Our choice would be one for you, one for me. So, from the four states, two should be for them, two for us,” said Mohamad in his winding-up speech at the 2026 Umno assembly today.
Umno-led Barisan Nasional currently governs Negeri Sembilan together with PAS, with the former holding 18 seats and the latter seven.
Mohamad also reminded Melaka Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh to negotiate seat distribution with political partners without compromising Umno’s dignity ahead of the next state election.
The current Melaka state assembly’s term expires in December this year, but Ab Rauf has floated the possibility of dissolving it sooner.
“Umno has never relied on the sympathy of other people. So, Umno needs to build its own strength without banking on other parties,” Mohamad said.

Title: RM60,000 versus RM500,000: Penang chief minister says still weighing DAP’s call for equal funding law
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Sept 12 — The Penang government is unlikely to table a proposed law guaranteeing equal constituency development funds (CDF) at the coming state legislative assembly sitting, due to time constraints.
Penang Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow said he had instructed the state legal adviser to prepare a draft enactment.
“It was presented at the state exco meeting on Wednesday,” he told reporters at a press conference after presenting the Penang2030 eighth-year report card at Holiday Inn Resort today.
He said the state government needed time to examine its details, adding that an engagement session with stakeholders would also be required.
“We have some more time to deliberate on it,” he said.
Chow was responding to DAP’s recent call for Penang to enact legislation ensuring equal development allocations for all state constituencies.
On September 8, DAP secretary-general Anthony Loke said the party’s central executive committee had resolved to ask the Penang government to introduce the law.
“CDF should be given equally, regardless of the political background of the elected representatives,” Loke said then.
He said the legislation would guarantee fair and equal treatment for all Penang assemblymen, irrespective of political affiliation, and that the same principle should be extended to the federal level and adopted by every state government.
The Penang government currently provides each opposition assemblyman with RM60,000 annually, while government assemblymen receive RM500,000 in yearly constituency allocations.
Last August, Chow said the state would await a decision from DAP’s national leadership before moving ahead with such legislation.
He said Penang had provided allocations to opposition representatives for many years, although they had repeatedly sought higher amounts during state assembly sittings.

Title: Kon Yeow orders excos to clear unfinished Penang2030 projects before he steps down as chief minister
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Sept 12 — Penang Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow has ordered all state executive councillors to identify Penang2030 initiatives under their portfolios that have not been started or completed.
He said the directive was issued several weeks ago, and that he was personally monitoring the outstanding initiatives.
“I have given an order a few weeks ago for every exco to list down things that they have not completed, and I hope that they will take action to complete it.
“I want to hand over Penang nicely to the successor,” he told reporters after presenting the Penang2030 eighth-year report card at the Holiday Inn Resort here today.
Chow said he would seek explanations from state excos overseeing portfolios that had recorded slow progress.
Asked to rate his administration’s performance this term, he gave his standard reply of 70 per cent.
About eight in 10 key Penang2030 targets had either been achieved or were progressing, he said, covering areas including welfare and housing assistance, local government reform, tourism, education, agriculture, entrepreneurship and youth development.
He identified agriculture as one area requiring further improvement.
“Penang has established 384 urban farms, but agricultural productivity remains below the state’s target,” he said during his presentation.
The initial target had been to establish 100 urban farms; once that was achieved, the target was raised to 500, he said.
The state intends to expand technology-assisted methods such as smart agriculture, precision farming and vertical farming, drawing on Penang’s electrical and electronics industry and engineering talent.
Reducing household water consumption was another target the state has struggled to hit.
“If we can cut at least 28 litres, or ideally 55 litres to 220 litres per person per day, that is considered a win for us already,” he said.
He said the national average currently stands at 225 litres per capita daily, against the World Health Organisation’s recommended 165 litres.
“There is still much to be done. There is always much to be done because a government’s job is never done,” Chow said.
“Today is not a celebration. Today is for us to look back so we can orientate ourselves forward more precisely.”
He said several major infrastructure projects would continue beyond 2030, adding that he would leave it to his successor to decide whether existing programmes should be maintained or replaced with new priorities.

Title: Male elephant roaming near Terengganu village caught, now on a banana diet
Article:
KUALA BERANG, Sept 12 — The Terengganu Department of Wildlife and National Parks (Perhilitan) captured a wild male elephant that was roaming in Kampung Kolam, Ajil, near here on Thursday.
Its director, Dennis Ten Choon Yung said the animal, which had a paw print size of 15 inches (0.381 metres), was captured by six Perhilitan members before being tethered at the same location around 5.30 pm.
He said the elephant would be fed banana trunks twice a day by the department staff before being relocated to a suitable location.
On Sept 10, the Hulu Terengganu Wildlife Department office received a report regarding a wild elephant roaming in Kampung Kolam. On the same day, department staff conducted a capture operation and successfully caught the elephant.
“The capture will reduce the residents’ concerns about the safety threat posed by the wild animal involved,” he said in a statement today.
In this regard, he said his team reminded the public not to approach the area to avoid noise that would stress the elephant. — Bernama
*Editor’s note: Perhilitan stands for Jabatan Perlindungan Hidupan Liar dan Taman Negara, the Malay name for the Department of Wildlife and National Parks.

Title: Nurses wanted: Public Service Commission says 400 posts still open despite hiring push
Article:
KUALA KANGSAR, Sept 12 — The Public Service Commission (SPA) has filled more than 1,000 nursing vacancies in the public service to date, with open interviews being conducted to expedite the recruitment process.
Its chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Jailani Muhamed Yunus said the move was among its immediate efforts to address the need to fill critical posts, particularly nurses, who are in high demand in the healthcare sector.
“To date, we need more than 1,400 (nurses) and we have already filled more than 1,000. So, we still need several hundred more to be filled urgently.
“These efforts are ongoing from time to time because there are also nursing positions that require candidates to undergo training, and this training takes time,” he told reporters after officiating at the SPA Madani Adopted Village Project Handover Ceremony at Kampung Orang Asli Ulu Chenein here today.
Also present were Department of Orang Asli Development Director-General Muhammad Akmal Ila Ahmad, SPA Secretary Datuk Ikhbal Hanam Mukras and Kampung Orang Asli Ulu Chenein village head Din Alang.
Ahmad Jailani said the open interview and walk-in methods were introduced early this year through several career carnivals organised by SPA nationwide, providing more opportunities for qualified youths to join the public service.
He said candidates with a diploma in nursing could walk in for an interview, while those who had yet to submit an online application could also complete their SPA application at the interview centre before attending the session.
“This is also a breakthrough effort that we have undertaken to expedite the process. If we use the usual process, there may sometimes be delays. Apart from nurses, SPA is also focusing on filling several other critical positions that require urgent recruitment, including Public Health Assistants.
“The demand for nurses is quite high, particularly as the healthcare industry has become increasingly important in the country. Therefore, the target is usually (recruiting) nurses into the public service, as the possibly better offers in the private sector mean that a large proportion of them join (the private sector) rather than the public service,” he said.
Meanwhile, Ahmad Jailani, who is also chairman of the Judicial and Legal Service Commission, said the government did not prevent civil servants from seeking better employment opportunities after completing their contracts but instead, SPA would ensure that succession plans were implemented by continuously recruiting new personnel.
“They have contracts that have been stipulated in their appointments. However, once their contracts expire, they are free. We cannot prevent any government officers from seeking better employment opportunities.
“So, there are no restrictions in this regard and we give them the freedom to do so. Nevertheless, we believe the important thing is the succession plan, and we will find ways to recruit new personnel. I am confident that if we go to places such as Felda Chenein in Lenggong, we can find youths who want to join the service,” he said. — Bernama
*Editor’s note: The initials SPA stand for Suruhanjaya Perkhidmatan Awam, the Public Service Commission’s name in Malay.

Title: Come set up shop in KL, Anwar says to  Ethiopia after decades apart
Article:
NEW DELHI, Sept 12 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim extended an invitation to Ethiopia to establish an Embassy in Kuala Lumpur during his bilateral meeting with his counterpart, Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed.
Malaysia’s reopening of its embassy in Addis Ababa in September 2025, after 43 years, marked significant progress in bilateral relations.
The discussion also touched on the positive momentum generated by reciprocal visits by both leaders. Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed visited Malaysia in 2024, while Anwar visited Ethiopia in 2025.
The Prime Minister said it has been agreed that the first Bilateral Consultation will take place in Kuala Lumpur next year to further strengthen cooperation between the two countries.
Other areas of cooperation discussed included halal products, agriculture, food security, pharmaceuticals, digital services, renewable energy and tourism.
Anwar also expressed his appreciation for Ethiopia’s support for Malaysia’s engagement with Brics during the bilateral meeting that took place on the sidelines of the 18th Brics Leaders’ Summit here.
Malaysia’s participation in the Summit is in its capacity as a Brics Partner Country, a status it has held since Jan 1, 2025.
Ethiopia, the world’s most populous landlocked country, ranked as Malaysia’s 26th-largest trading partner in the African continent in 2023.
Bilateral trade between Malaysia and Ethiopia stood at RM446.8 million in 2023, with Malaysia’s exports to Ethiopia valued at RM358.6 million, representing a 24.6 per cent increase from the previous year. — Bernama
* Editor’s note: Brics is a bloc of major emerging economies that originally comprised Brazil, Russia, India, China and South Africa, but has since expanded to include countries such as Ethiopia, Egypt, Iran and the UAE.

Title: As new law on campus politics takes shape, minister sorts students into two camps — ‘Agree’ and ‘Disagree’
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 12 — Discussions are under way with all relevant parties on the drafting of a new law to replace the Universities and University Colleges Act 1971 (UUCA), said Higher Education Minister Datuk Seri Dr Zambry Abdul Kadir.
He said several meetings had been held with representatives of the academic community and university administrators, while discussions with other groups, including students, would continue over the coming days.
“I have already met with Student Representative Councils and asked the National Student Representative Council, which represents students from all universities, to organise their own groups, whether Group A or Group B, representing those who agree and disagree, so that we can bring the views together and consider them.
“This is because I want the new law to be comprehensive,” he told reporters while visiting the Media Lounge in conjunction with the 2026 Umno General Assembly at the World Trade Centre Kuala Lumpur here today.
He said the new law should not only take into account current needs, but also address the challenges the country may face in the future.
Zambry said this is important as the UUCA, introduced in 1971, covers various aspects of higher education institutions, including the establishment and administration of universities, as well as matters concerning students.
Against this backdrop, he said, changes in the higher education landscape and the current legal framework need to be taken into account when drafting the new law.
“I have said repeatedly that UUCA was introduced 54 years ago. There have obviously been changes, and some may say that it is no longer suitable,” he said.
In August, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the government would repeal UUCA in its entirety, with a Bill on the matter to be tabled in Parliament this year.
Anwar said the proposal to repeal the Act aimed to give student movements in the country greater freedom and democratic space, after taking into account memoranda and views from student leaders, who wanted comprehensive changes to the Act. — Bernama

Title: NSE southbound lane near Menora Tunnel reopens after slope deemed safe
Article:
IPOH, Sept 12 — The left lane of the North-South Expressway (NSE) southbound at KM263.6, which was temporarily closed following a landslide yesterday, has been reopened to all vehicles at 1pm today.
Perak police chief Datuk Mohd Alwi Zainal Abidin said technical assessments by the relevant authorities found the slope at the location to be safe.
“As such, the southbound left lane was reopened to all vehicles at 1pm. Traffic in both directions is currently reported to be flowing smoothly.
“Repair works on the slope will continue to ensure that the area remains safe,” he said in a statement today.
He also advised motorists to exercise caution when passing through the area, comply with safety instructions and signages and reduce their speed, especially during rain or bad weather.
Earlier, the left lane at the landslide site at KM263.6 of the North-South Expressway (southbound) was closed, spanning about one kilometre.
Yesterday, the Malaysian Highway Authority (LLM) reported that a slope collapse at KM263.6 of the North-South Expressway (southbound) — between the Menora Tunnel and Ipoh — had caused a traffic jam stretching 15km. — Bernama

Title: From speech to GE16 manifesto: BN locks in Blue Malaysia Agenda
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 12 — The Blue Malaysia Agenda outlined by Umno president Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi will be reflected in Barisan Nasional’s (BN) manifesto for the 16th General Election (GE16), says BN secretary-general Datuk Seri Dr Zambry Abd Kadir.
He said the agenda formed part of the coalition’s efforts to formulate an approach that ensured Malaysia remained peaceful and stable, while navigating current and future challenges.
“The president outlined eight initiatives under the Blue Malaysia Agenda… all of which are crucial to ensuring the nation stays peaceful and stable, while demonstrating our resolve to address current challenges.
“For instance, amid an increasingly volatile global landscape, careful planning is required to ensure Malaysia remains peaceful and prosperous,” he told reporters at the Media Centre during the Umno General Assembly 2026 at the World Trade Centre Kuala Lumpur today.
Yesterday, Ahmad Zahid said Umno and BN would outline the Blue Malaysia Agenda to shape the nation’s trajectory heading towards the centenary of its independence, should the coalition return to lead Putrajaya.
The agenda carries aspirations to build a sovereign and united Malaysia, an innovative and high-income nation, a prosperous and equitable society, and a globally respected country. — Bernama

Title: Anwar-Modi Brics meeting: Semiconductor ties, bilateral trade take centre stage
Article:
NEW DELHI, Sept 12 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim and his Indian counterpart Narendra Modi discussed deepening semiconductor cooperation and translating it into industry partnerships during their bilateral meeting here today.
Anwar spoke about integrated supply chains, talent development and two-way investment during the meeting held on the sidelines of the 18th Brics Leaders’ Summit.
Anwar, who is also the Finance Minister, reaffirmed Malaysia’s commitment to increasing bilateral trade and investment, enhancing cooperation across various sectors, as well as implementing measures to facilitate and expedite Malaysian exports to India.
The Prime Minister also spoke on exploring opportunities to further strengthen tourism and people-to-people ties through increased flight connectivity.
He expressed his appreciation for the warm welcome and reaffirmed the longstanding friendship between Malaysia and India.
Anwar arrived here yesterday to attend the Summit hosted by Modi. This is his second visit to India with the first in August 2024.
Malaysia is participating in the Summit in its capacity as a Brics Partner Country, a status it has held since January 1, 2025.
The two countries have maintained long-standing relations since 1957. Their bilateral ties were elevated to a comprehensive strategic partnership during Anwar’s first visit to the republic.
India remains Malaysia’s largest trading partner in the South Asian region, with total trade between the two countries reaching RM79.49 billion (US$18.59 billion) in 2025.
Malaysia’s key exports to India comprise palm oil and palm oil-based agricultural products, as well as electrical and electronic products, while imports mainly comprise agricultural, petroleum and chemical products. — Bernama

Title: ‘My brother’: PM Anwar, Modi meet on Brics sidelines
Article:
NEW DELHI, Sept 12 — “My brother” had the rare honour of becoming the warm greeting between Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim and his Indian counterpart Narendra Modi at their bilateral meeting here today.
The two leaders met on the sidelines of the 18th Bric Leaders’ Summit at the Hyderabad House, which is the State Guest House under the Ministry of External Affairs.
It is used for bilateral meetings, state banquets and meetings with foreign leaders.
Malaysia is participating in the Summit as a Brics Partner Country, a status it has held since January 1, 2025.
Anwar arrived here yesterday to attend the Summit hosted by Modi. This is his second visit to India, following his first in August 2024.
Malaysia and India have maintained long-standing relations since 1957, which were elevated to a Comprehensive Strategic Partnership during the Prime Minister’s first visit here.
India remains Malaysia’s largest trading partner in the South Asian region, with total trade between the two countries reaching RM79.49 billion in 2025.
Malaysia’s key export items comprised palm oil and palm oil-based agricultural products, as well as electrical and electronic products, while imports mainly consisted of agricultural, petroleum and chemical products. — Bernama

Title: A spring in Umno’s step: Three things we learnt from its 2026 general assembly
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 12 — Umno’s annual general assembly ended yesterday with a sense of optimism rarely seen at the party’s recent assemblies, as delegates filled the World Trade Centre Kuala Lumpur with renewed enthusiasm for the party.
The four-day assembly was also notable for Umno’s warm welcome to PAS delegates, although some members remained wary of the latter’s history of political partnerships that eventually fell apart.
Here are three things we learnt from this year’s assembly.
Umno members gather for the opening of the 2026 Umno General Assembly at the World Trade Centre Kuala Lumpur on September 11, 2026. — Picture by Sayuti Zainudin
1. Sky-high confidence among Umno delegates
The mood at the World Trade Centre here was noticeably different this year.
A week before the assembly began, Umno secretary-general Datuk Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki described it as a “Hari Raya Umno” for delegates, and the mood inside the venue did not disappoint.
Just outside the WTC entrance, buskers were seen performing Umno’s anthem, “Bersatu, Bersetia, Berkhidmat”, with delegates singing along as they went in and out of the building.
Delegates were constantly taking photographs and recording videos around the venue, with some cheering as they gathered in the main foyer.
When the debates began in Dewan Merdeka, many delegates gathered in front of the big screen at the main stage and listened intently.
The party’s membership counter was also consistently busy, with members queuing to collect their cards while others waited to register as new members.
The rows of shops around the venue were similarly lively, with delegates browsing and making purchases between sessions.
Umno members wave party flags during the opening of the 2026 Umno General Assembly at the World Trade Centre Kuala Lumpur on September 11, 2026. — Picture by Sayuti Zainudin
The mood was a far cry from some of Umno’s recent assemblies, which were held against the backdrop of electoral defeats, internal divisions and uncertainty over the party’s place in national politics.
Even the previous assembly, held in January this year, lacked the same sense of optimism and confidence.
This time, delegates arrived fresh from Umno and Barisan Nasional’s (BN) strong performances in Johor and Negeri Sembilan.
Datin Seri Rosmah Mansor arrives for the 2026 Umno General Assembly at the World Trade Centre Kuala Lumpur on September 11, 2026. — Picture by Raymond Manuel
BN won 48 of the 56 seats in Johor, including 36 for Umno, while in Negeri Sembilan the coalition secured 18 of the 36 seats, with Umno winning all 16 seats it contested.
Those victories appear to have given the party something it has struggled to maintain since its defeat in the 2018 general election: confidence that it can win again.
2. PAS is being welcomed back, despite its history
Perhaps the most striking political development at this year’s assembly was the warm reception given to PAS delegates.
When the first PAS representatives arrived at the assembly on Wednesday night, they were greeted by Umno members, with deputy president Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan even asking three PAS Muslimat delegates: “Kayfa haluka?”, or “How are you?” in Arabic.
The gesture came after Umno leaders attended PAS’ annual muktamar the previous week, with Asyraf saying PAS’ top leadership had been invited to the Umno assembly as a reciprocal gesture.
For a party whose relationship with PAS has swung from cooperation to bitter rivalry and back again, the warmth was significant.
Umno leaders have also repeatedly made clear that they are open to cooperation with other Malay parties, but not at the expense of the party’s own interests or identity.
That message was echoed by Umno delegates, some of whom said the past should remain in the past, but PAS would have to show that it could be a different partner this time around.
There is good reason for that caution. Umno and PAS previously worked together under Muafakat Nasional before their relationship deteriorated, while PAS later became a key component of Perikatan Nasional and contested against Umno.
Some Umno delegates have also pointed to PAS’ previous political partnerships through Pakatan Rakyat and with Bersatu in Perikatan Nasional as reminders that political cooperation can be short-lived.
Umno Youth chief Datuk Dr Muhamad Akmal Saleh and PAS Youth chief Afnan Hamimi Taib Azamudeen pose together during the Umno Youth annual general assembly at the World Trade Centre Kuala Lumpur on September 10, 2026. — Picture by Yusof Isa
So while the door to PAS is clearly open again, Umno is making clear that any cooperation must be on mutually agreed terms, with neither side turning on the other when political circumstances change.
The underlying message from the assembly appears simple: if Umno and PAS are going to work together again, this time there should be no backstabbing.
The next test could come in Melaka, where Umno Youth chief Datuk Dr Muhamad Akmal Saleh has said his wing is ready to work with PAS, describing the state election as a test of whether “penyatuan ummah” can become an electoral strategy rather than remain merely an idea.
3. Umno is already eyeing a return to federal power
If there was one message that came through most strongly from the assembly, it was that Umno wants to be seen as more than just a component of the current Unity Government.
Zahid called for GE16 to be held “as soon as possible”, telling delegates that the election would be a defining moment for Umno and BN to regain the mandate to lead the country.
During the debate on the president’s policy speech, Kedah Umno delegate Datuk Shaiful Hazizy Zainol Abidin singled out several PH ministers, including Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek, Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil, Dr Mohammed Taufiq Johari and Nga Kor Ming, along with DAP as a whole, describing them as “illnesses”.
“What is the medicine for these illnesses? What is the medicine to save the country? The medicine is to return the mandate to the people. An election must be held immediately,” he said.
Zahid described Melaka as the next battleground for the coalition’s “blue wave” strategy.
He also laid out eight initiatives for BN to pursue should it return to Putrajaya after GE16.
A delegate wipes away tears during the opening of the 2026 UMNO General Assembly at the World Trade Centre (WTC) in Kuala Lumpur. September 11, 2026 — Picture by Raymond Manuel
Among them was Zahid’s pledge that state institutions would not be used as political tools if BN returned to power.
Former Umno Youth chief Khairy Jamaluddin later described the speech as sounding like that of a “PM in waiting”.
The message was also apparent in the party’s discussions about its position within the Unity Government.
Mohamad acknowledged that Umno had struggled to convince Malay voters to accept its cooperation with DAP, saying long-standing perceptions of DAP continued to shape how the partnership was viewed.
At the same time, he said Umno would remain “forever centrist”, while stressing the importance of Malay unity and the party’s Rumah Bangsa concept.
Taken together, the messages suggest that Umno is trying to position itself for the next phase of national politics: retaining its place in government for now, while increasingly talking about what it would do if voters return BN to power after GE16.

Title: ‘We still have until February 2028’, Pakatan sec-gen says as GE16 chatter grows
Article:
PEKAN, Sept 12 — Pakatan Harapan secretary-general Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail today brushed aside calls for the 16th general election to be held earlier, saying the Madani government’s term only expires in February 2028.
Saifuddin Nasution was responding to questions from reporters after officiating the launch of the 2026 Madani Adopted Village and School by the Immigration Department at Sekolah Kebangsaan Nenasi here, national news agency
Bernama
reported.
“We still have until February 2028… there are many more things we can do by leveraging our position in the government, maintaining stability, managing the economy prudently and focusing on the welfare of the people,” he was quoted saying.
“More than a year is ample time for us to focus on fulfilling our responsibilities as leaders and safeguarding the people's welfare. In my view, that is more important,” he added.
Speculation over GE16’s timing has intensified in recent months, even though Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim's administration is not required to call the polls until Parliament automatically dissolves in December 2027, with an election to follow within 60 days after that.
Anwar is from the same party and coalition as Saifuddin Nasution.
Political analysts have floated several possible windows for an early dissolution, including the final quarter of 2026 to align with a cluster of state elections in Melaka, Sarawak and Johor, or shortly after Budget 2027 is tabled.
Some observers have also linked the timing to internal coalition dynamics that could trigger a chain of events leading to dissolution as early as February 2027.
Anwar has previously signalled that Parliament could be dissolved earlier than scheduled if coalition partners act in ways that threaten political stability — a remark made after Umno and the Barisan Nasional coalition it leads decided to contest solo in all Johor seats during that state’s own polls.
The Election Commission has said it remains fully prepared for any early dissolution of state assemblies or a snap GE16, amid the persistent speculation.

Title: Were the 30 Malaysians caught in Indonesia lone scammers, or something bigger? Home Ministry to dig deeper
Article:
PEKAN, Sept 12 — Malaysia will conduct an investigation following the detention of 30 Malaysians suspected of being involved in online scam activities in Pontianak, West Kalimantan, Indonesia.
Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said the country’s authorities would take appropriate action regarding the matter.
“The usual practice is for the Indonesian authorities to contact our police force to allow us to conduct an investigation from our perspective.
“The purpose is to establish whether this was an operation involving only these 30 individuals acting independently or whether they were part of a more organised syndicate. The information obtained will enable us to formulate a plan for further action,” he said.
He said this at a media conference after officiating the launch of the 2026 Madani Adopted Village and School by the Immigration Department at Sekolah Kebangsaan Nenasi here today.
It was reported that Indonesian authorities detained 30 Malaysians and a Taiwanese national at a hotel at about 11.15 am on Tuesday following intelligence on suspicious activities involving foreign nationals.
Meanwhile, Saifuddin Nasution, who is also Pakatan Harapan secretary-general, said the Madani Government’s focus was currently on prioritising issues affecting the people.
“We still have until February 2028… there are many more things we can do by leveraging our position in the government, maintaining stability, managing the economy prudently and focusing on the welfare of the people.
“More than a year is ample time for us to focus on fulfilling our responsibilities as leaders and safeguarding the people’s welfare. In my view, that is more important,” he said.
He said this when asked to comment on calls for the 16th General Election to be held earlier, before the current parliamentary term expires. — Bernama

Title: Anwar to Iran: Keep Hormuz open, choose diplomacy over conflict
Article:
NEW DELHI, Sept 12 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim expressed concern over the continued conflict and escalation across West Asia during a bilateral meeting with Iran President Masoud Pezeshkian today.
Anwar, who is here for the 18th BRICS Leaders’ Summit, reiterates the importance of maintaining the freedom and safety of maritime passage through the Strait of Hormuz in accordance with international law.
“Malaysia urged all parties to return to dialogue and diplomacy to resolve disputes and de-escalate the situation,” the prime minister said during a 30-minute meeting between the two leaders on the sidelines of the summit here.
Anwar, who is also finance minister, welcomed Putrajaya and Tehran’s long-standing diplomatic relations and reaffirmed cooperation on various fronts.
He also called on a continuation and expansion of trade and investment cooperation and opportunities, especially in energy, agriculture, palm oil, food security, halal, technology, and higher education. — Bernama

Title: Mission done, but not over: Smart team on way home as Nepal search continues
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 12 — The Special Malaysia Disaster Assistance and Rescue Team (Smart), which participated in the Humanitarian Assistance and Disaster Relief mission in Nepal, is expected to return home today or tomorrow, said Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan.
He stated that all equipment belonging to the team, such as drones, has been handed over to rescue teams in Nepal for use in search operations for flood victims in the country.
“Nepalese authorities do not intend (at this time) to announce the termination of search and rescue (SAR) operations, as there are still 5,000 people unaccounted for.
“The Smart team leader will provide a report and assess the next steps so that we do not make hasty decisions; if they (Nepal) require assistance from Malaysia, we can consider helping with the search or rescue operations,” he said.
Mohamad told reporters while visiting the Media Centre at the 2026 Umno General Assembly here today.
The Smart MAS01 team, participating in the Humanitarian Assistance and Disaster Relief mission to Nepal, arrived in the country via Tribhuvan International Airport, Kathmandu, on September 5.
The team, comprising 11 personnel and officers, departed for Nepal on a Royal Malaysian Air Force A400M aircraft from the RMAF Subang Air Base, carrying 12.4 tonnes of SAR equipment.
Meanwhile, Mohamad stated that the Malaysian Embassy in Kathmandu is in constant contact with the Nepalese government to obtain the latest information regarding the status of Malaysians reported missing in the tragedy.
He said this is to enable next-of-kin to handle matters such as insurance claims and other related issues.
“In Nepal, for anyone reported missing or unaccounted for, a death certificate can be issued after three years, whereas in Malaysia, it takes seven years.
“That is why we have asked the (Malaysian) embassy there to liaise with the (Nepalese) ministry to determine how next-of-kin can obtain documents confirming the status of the Malaysians who remain missing,” he said. — Bernama

Title: After Bandar Tasik Selatan PPR gets RM350,000 makeover, MP asks residents to ‘take good care’ for sake of kids and grandkids
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 12 — A total of RM350,000 has been allocated for road upgrading works at Pangsapuri Kos Rendah Bandar Tasik Selatan here under the 2026 Projek Mesra Rakyat initiative.
Bandar Tun Razak Member of Parliament Datuk Seri Dr Wan Azizah Wan Ismail said repair works on the lifts at the apartments would also be carried out soon to ensure residents’ comfort.
“Once upgraded, please take good care of these facilities. We must work together to develop and maintain them so that our children and grandchildren can also enjoy the benefits,” she said while officiating the Bandar Tun Razak Parliamentary Constituency Kenduri Rakyat Madani 2026 programme here today.
At the same event, the Prime Minister’s wife also launched a RM72,000 Flexi EV charging station comprising four electric vehicle charging units at the apartment complex.
She said the project was implemented in collaboration with the apartment’s management corporation, Leading Innovative Technologies & Systems Sdn Bhd and Pro Parking Sdn Bhd.
Dr Wan Azizah said the initiative demonstrated how collaboration among the community, management bodies and the private sector could deliver better facilities for residents.
She also urged residents to make full use of the available facilities and services while working together to address community issues.
Dr Wan Azizah also presented Ember AI tuition sponsorships to 10 Form Five students who will sit for the Sijil Pelajaran Malaysia examination this year.
She also stressed the need to ensure children receive adequate nutrition to support their growth, particularly amid the challenges of urban living.
The Special Kenduri Rakyat Madani satellite programme aims to foster closer ties between leaders, government agencies and the local community while bringing government information and services closer to the people.
More than 1,000 local residents attended the programme organised by the Information Department, which featured Jualan Rahmah and Jualan Agro Madani, as well as health check-ups, mammogram services and anaemia screenings.
After the event, Dr Wan Azizah visited the family of a woman caring for her ailing parents at Block A of the apartment and handed over contributions from the Social Security Organisation and the Federal Territories Islamic Religious Council.
Afiqah Ramli @ Mohd Yusoff, 32, has been caring for her bedridden mother, Sharifah Norol Ashikin Syed Abdullah, 64, who suffered an aneurysm, while also attending to her father, Ramli @ Mohd Yusoff Daharon, 61, following his stent insertion procedure and heart bypass surgery.
The Universiti Teknologi MARA graduate, formerly a credit control executive at a company in Cameron Highlands, left her job to care for both her parents full-time.
“We have to cover transportation costs for medical appointments, treatment for bedsores and the monthly replacement of my mother’s feeding tube, on top of the family’s daily expenses.
“Caring for both my parents has affected my health. I have back pain that spreads to my shoulders and legs, and I find it difficult to move around without painkillers,” she told Bernama.
The second of three siblings thanked Dr Wan Azizah for taking the time to visit her family. — Bernama

Title: Foreign Ministry seeks DNA samples of Nepal flood victims to identify missing Malaysians
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 12 — Malaysia is reportedly in talks with Nepal to have DNA samples from flood victims found during search-and-rescue operations sent here for matching against samples taken from relatives of Malaysians who remain missing, Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan said today.
According to
Utusan Malaysia
, Mohamad said the initiative was proposed because Nepalese authorities face shortages of facilities and equipment needed to identify victims.
“Send them here so it will be easier for us to carry out matching with close family members whose DNA samples have already been taken,” he was quoted as saying.
Mohamad reportedly said Malaysia was also considering sending DNA experts to Nepal, while the Malaysian Embassy in Kathmandu has asked Nepalese security authorities to forward samples already collected from recovered victims.
He said the proposal had been submitted to the Nepalese government and Malaysia was awaiting a response.
Mohamad said Malaysia is also discussing with Nepal ways to help families of missing Malaysians obtain documents needed for matters such as insurance claims.
At last count, 55 Malaysians remained missing following the August 26 floods and landslides in Nepal.

Title: Umno won’t ‘betray anyone’ or seek new PM before next general election, says Asyraf Wajdi
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 12 — Umno secretary-general Datuk Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki today said the party would not seek to change the prime minister or form a new government before the next general election is called.
He said Umno remained committed to political stability and had yet to begin negotiations for the next general election.
“As long as the elections are not called, we will not ‘tebuk atap’ (form a backdoor government) or seek to change the prime minister,” he told reporters at a press conference on the sidelines of the 2026 Umno General Assembly today.
“We have not started negotiations for the next election. Talks will only begin after Parliament is dissolved, just as they did after the state legislative assemblies in Johor and Negeri Sembilan were dissolved,” he said.
Asyraf Wajdi was responding to questions about remarks by Umno president Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi, who yesterday appeared to criticise Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim’s past election promise to rein in petrol prices within 24 hours and the flip-flop over the Budi95 fuel subsidy quota.
While the Umno-led Barisan Nasional (BN) sits with Pakatan Harapan in the federal government, it governs Negeri Sembilan with Islamist party PAS.
Speculation over Umno strengthening political ties with PAS intensified after PAS secretary-general Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan and several other senior party leaders attended the Umno General Assembly yesterday.
Asyraf Wajdi also refuted claims that Umno would be committing a “betrayal” by seeking political cooperation with other parties.
“Umno isn’t betraying anyone. The agreement (to form the unity government) is only applicable until the next general election is called.
“After that, all parties are free to choose their own directions. I don’t expect even Sabah and Sarawak to want to be dictated to on who they should cooperate with,” he said.
